# Quick Files Converter — complete reference

> Full detail for AI assistants. For the concise version see /llms.txt.

## Site summary

Quick Files Converter (https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/) is a free file-conversion website with 93 online tools. Every tool converts files entirely on the visitor's device using web technology (Canvas, WebAssembly, File API) — there is no server-side processing, no database, no user accounts, no sign-up and no watermarks. Tool categories: PDF Converters (20 tools), Image Converters (27 tools), Text Converters (5 tools), Data Converters (7 tools), Subtitle Converters (12 tools), Video Converters (12 tools), Audio Converters (9 tools), File Tools (1 tool). Flagship tools include the Video to GIF Maker, Edit PDF, Merge PDF, Compress PDF, HEIC to JPG and MP4 to MP3. Privacy policy: files never leave the visitor's device; nothing is uploaded anywhere; the "Summarize with AI" buttons only share a page's public summary text with the chosen AI, never the visitor's files.

## PDF Converters

Free online PDF tools that run entirely in your browser. Turn JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and HEIC images, TXT, Markdown and CSV files into PDF documents — or convert PDF to JPG/PNG images, merge, split, compress, rotate, watermark, add page numbers, redact, crop, delete pages, unlock and edit PDFs, and extract text and images — your documents are never uploaded anywhere.

### PDF to JPG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/pdf-to-jpg/

What it does:
Convert every page of a PDF into crisp JPG images — download pages individually or all at once as a ZIP. Perfect for sharing document pages as images, posting to social media, or pulling figures out of a report.

About the source format (PDF):
PDF is the universal document format — contracts, ebooks, reports and forms. But PDF pages can’t be posted as images or opened in every photo app.

About the target format (JPG):
JPG is the world’s most compatible image format. As page images, your document opens anywhere — phones, social apps, email and websites that don’t accept PDFs.

Use cases:
- Sharing a document page as an image on WhatsApp or social media
- Extracting charts and figures from a PDF report
- Converting PDF pages for a presentation when the venue PC has no PDF reader

Tip: Pages render at double resolution (2x) so text stays sharp — and each JPG downloads individually, so you can grab just the pages you need.

FAQs:
Q: How do I turn PDF pages into JPG images?
A: Drop your PDF above and hit convert. Each page renders as a high-resolution JPG you can download individually — or grab every page at once as a ZIP file. Everything happens in your browser; the PDF is never uploaded.

Q: What resolution are the JPG images?
A: Each page renders at 2x scale — roughly 1700×2200 px for a standard A4 page — so text stays crisp even when zoomed.

Q: Can I download all pages at once?
A: Yes — "Download all as ZIP" gives you every page image in one file, or download pages individually.

Q: Is there a page limit?
A: PDFs up to 150 pages convert in the browser. For larger documents, split them first with our free Split PDF tool.

Q: Do password-protected PDFs work?
A: No — the browser version cannot open password-protected PDFs. Remove the password in your desktop PDF reader first, then convert.

Q: PDF to JPG or PDF to PNG?
A: JPG for the smallest files (great for sharing); PNG when you need pixel-perfect quality for print or archiving.

### PDF to PNG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/pdf-to-png/

What it does:
Convert PDF pages to lossless PNG images at high resolution. Choose PNG when every pixel matters — print, archiving, or documents with fine text and diagrams.

About the source format (PDF):
PDF pages mix text, vector graphics and images in one document. When you need a page as a picture with no quality compromise, PNG is the answer.

About the target format (PNG):
PNG preserves every pixel exactly — the right choice for print, archiving, and documents where fine text must stay perfectly legible.

Use cases:
- Archiving important document pages as pixel-perfect images
- Extracting diagrams from a PDF for a print publication
- Converting pages for OCR software that prefers PNG input

Tip: PNGs are bigger than JPGs — if you are just sharing on chat, PDF to JPG gives much smaller files.

FAQs:
Q: Why convert PDF pages to PNG instead of JPG?
A: PNG is lossless — text edges and diagrams stay razor-sharp with zero compression artifacts. Files are bigger than JPG, but quality is pixel-perfect.

Q: How big will the PNG files be?
A: Bigger than JPG — a full A4 page at 2x can be 1–3 MB. That is the price of lossless quality.

Q: Does PNG keep the text selectable?
A: No — the output is an image of the page. Use our PDF to Text tool if you need the actual words.

### JPG to PDF Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/jpg-to-pdf/

What it does:
Turn JPG photos and scans into a single PDF document — one image per page, in the order you choose. The classic fix for "please send it as a PDF".

About the source format (JPG):
JPGs are how phones save photos and scans — but offices, universities and forms almost always ask for PDF.

About the target format (PDF):
PDF packages your images into one professional document that prints cleanly and opens identically everywhere.

Use cases:
- Turning phone photos of documents into a single PDF for email
- Combining scanned pages into one file for a job or visa application
- Converting JPG screenshots into a PDF report

Tip: Drop multiple JPGs at once — they become pages in order. Quality 92 is perfect for documents; go lower if the PDF must stay tiny for upload forms.

FAQs:
Q: How do I combine JPG images into one PDF?
A: Drop your JPGs above — pick several at once — arrange them if needed, set quality, and download a single PDF with one image per page. All in your browser, nothing uploaded.

Q: Can I add multiple JPGs to one PDF?
A: Yes — select several images at once and each becomes a page, in the order shown. This is the main reason people use this tool.

Q: What page size will the PDF use?
A: Each page matches its image’s dimensions, so nothing is stretched or cropped — photos keep their exact aspect ratio.

Q: How do I keep the PDF small for uploads?
A: Lower the quality slider to 70–80. For scanned documents the difference is invisible and the file shrinks dramatically.

Q: JPG to PDF or PNG to PDF?
A: JPG to PDF for photos and scans (smaller). PNG to PDF when the images have sharp text you cannot afford to soften.

Q: Will the PDF look the same when printed?
A: Yes — each page is your image at full resolution, so printing reproduces it faithfully.

About the source format (PNG):
PNG is the format of screenshots and crisp graphics — lossless, but not what forms and offices accept.

About the target format (PDF):
PDF is the document standard: one file, printable, accepted by every institution and upload form.

Use cases:

- Turning design mockups into a presentable PDF

Tip: PNG sources stay sharp — the PDF embeds them at full quality, so text screenshots remain perfectly readable.

FAQs:

Q: Can I merge several PNGs into one PDF?
A: Yes — drop multiple PNGs and each becomes a page in order.

Q: Will transparency in my PNGs survive?

### Merge PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/merge-pdf/

What it does:
Combine multiple PDF files into one document — arrange pages in any order with up/down controls. The fastest way to join contracts, chapters or scanned batches.

About the source format (PDF):
PDFs arrive in pieces — separate chapters, scanned batches, a contract plus its annex. Reading or sending them one by one is a hassle.

About the target format (PDF):
One merged PDF reads front-to-back like a proper document and attaches to a single email instead of five.

Use cases:
- Joining a contract and its signed annex into one file
- Combining separately scanned chapters into a single ebook
- Merging monthly statements into one yearly PDF

Tip: Use the up/down arrows to set the final order before merging — the first file in the list becomes the first pages of the result.

FAQs:
Q: How do I merge two PDFs into one?
A: Drop both PDFs above, arrange them in the order you want with the up/down arrows, and download one combined PDF. The original files are never modified or uploaded.

Q: How many PDFs can I merge at once?
A: As many as your browser memory allows — a dozen typical documents merge in seconds. Truly huge files (hundreds of MB) may strain a phone browser.

Q: Does merging change quality?
A: No — pages are copied exactly as they are, with no re-rendering. Text stays selectable and vector graphics stay sharp.

Q: Can I remove a file before merging?
A: Yes — each file in the list has a remove button, plus up/down arrows to reorder.

Q: Will bookmarks or form fields survive merging?
A: Page content merges perfectly. Interactive form fields and bookmarks from the originals are not carried over in the browser version.

Q: Is there a file size limit?
A: No hard limit, but very large PDFs (500+ MB combined) can exhaust phone browser memory — merge those on a desktop.

### Split PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/split-pdf/

What it does:
Extract pages from a PDF — enter a range like "1-3, 5" and download just those pages as a new PDF. Pull one chapter out of a manual or one invoice out of a batch.

About the source format (PDF):
Big PDFs bundle everything together — but you often need just a chapter, a receipt, or three pages for a form.

About the target format (PDF):
A split PDF contains only the pages you asked for: smaller, focused, and ready to send.

Use cases:
- Pulling one invoice out of a monthly batch PDF
- Extracting a single chapter from an ebook
- Sending only the relevant pages of a long report

Tip: Page numbers start at 1 (the first page). Ranges like 1-3 and lists like 1-3, 5, 8-10 both work.

FAQs:
Q: How do I extract specific pages from a PDF?
A: Drop your PDF, type the pages you want — single pages like "5", ranges like "1-3", or combined "1-3, 5, 8-10" — and download a new PDF with exactly those pages.

Q: What page-range formats work?
A: Single pages ("5"), ranges ("1-3") and combinations ("1-3, 5, 8-10"). Pages are extracted in ascending order.

Q: Does splitting reduce quality?
A: No — pages are copied exactly, so text and images keep their original quality.

### Compress PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/compress-pdf/

What it does:
Shrink an oversized PDF so it fits email and upload limits. Re-compresses page images at High, Balanced or Small — best for scanned and image-heavy PDFs.

About the source format (PDF):
PDFs balloon when they are full of scanned images — a 40-page scan can be 100 MB, far over email and form limits.

About the target format (PDF):
A compressed PDF keeps every page readable at a fraction of the bytes — the same document, emailable again.

Use cases:
- Shrinking a scanned application to fit a 10 MB upload limit
- Making a photo-heavy PDF emailable
- Reducing a large ebook for phone storage

Tip: This works best on scanned/image PDFs. If your PDF is mostly text and already small, there is little left to squeeze — that is normal.

FAQs:
Q: How much smaller will my PDF get?
A: It depends on the PDF: scanned and image-heavy PDFs often shrink 50–80%, while text-only PDFs (already small) shrink less. Try "Balanced" first — it is the sweet spot.

Q: Will my text stay sharp?
A: At High and Balanced settings, yes for normal reading. "Smallest file" visibly softens fine print — use it only when size matters more than crispness.

Q: Honest note: how does this compression work?
A: It re-renders each page as an optimized image — that is why it excels on scanned PDFs and does little for text-only ones. Nothing is uploaded; it all happens on your device.

### PDF to Text Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/pdf-to-text/

What it does:
Extract all the text from a PDF into a clean .txt file. Copy quotes from ebooks, pull data from reports, or archive document content as plain text.

About the source format (PDF):
PDF text is trapped inside the document — copying it manually page by page is tedious and error-prone.

About the target format (Text):
Plain text is the universal editable format: searchable, quotable, and readable by every app ever made.

Use cases:
- Pulling quotes from an ebook for notes
- Extracting report text for analysis
- Archiving document content in a future-proof format

Tip: Tables and multi-column layouts extract as flowing text — great for reading, but don’t expect spreadsheet structure.

FAQs:
Q: How do I copy all text out of a PDF?
A: Drop the PDF and download a .txt file with the document’s text, page by page, paragraphs preserved. No selecting, no copy-paste marathons.

Q: What about scanned PDFs?
A: Scanned PDFs are pictures of text, not text — extraction finds nothing. Those need OCR, which the browser version doesn’t do yet.

Q: Is the reading order correct?
A: For normal single-column documents, yes. Complex multi-column magazine layouts may read out of order.

### PDF to Word Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/pdf-to-word/

What it does:
Extract your PDF’s text into an editable Word (.docx) document — free, in your browser. Honest note: this extracts the text; complex layouts, tables and images are not preserved.

About the source format (PDF):
PDFs lock text into fixed pages — great for reading, terrible when you need to edit, quote or reuse the words.

About the target format (Word):
A Word document frees the text: editable, reflowable, ready for your own formatting in Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice.

Use cases:
- Getting editable text out of a PDF report for rewriting
- Extracting contract text to quote in an email
- Turning an ebook chapter into an editable draft

Tip: Think of it as "text extraction", not "layout cloning" — the words come out clean and editable; the original design doesn’t.

FAQs:
Q: Is this a full PDF to Word conversion with layout?
A: Honest answer: no. This tool extracts the PDF’s text into a clean, editable Word document — headings detected, paragraphs preserved. Complex layouts, tables, images and exact formatting are not preserved. For pixel-perfect layout conversion you would need desktop software; for getting editable text out, this does the job in seconds.

Q: Why doesn’t it keep the exact layout?
A: True layout-preserving PDF-to-Word needs heavy desktop engines (and usually a server). Browsers can’t run those — so we do the honest version: clean, editable text. No fake promises.

Q: Will tables convert properly?
A: Table text extracts in reading order, but the table grid itself isn’t rebuilt. For data tables, PDF to Text plus manual cleanup works best.

Q: What about scanned PDFs?
A: Scanned PDFs contain images of text, not text — nothing extracts. They need OCR first, which the browser version doesn’t do yet.

Q: Can I open the .docx in Google Docs?
A: Yes — the file is a standard Word document and opens in Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice and WPS alike.

Q: Is my document uploaded anywhere?
A: Never. Extraction runs entirely in your browser — that is exactly why we offer the honest text version instead of a server round-trip.

### PDF to Excel Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/pdf-to-excel/

What it does:
Turn PDF tables into editable Excel spreadsheets — right in your browser. Bank statements, invoices, reports and price lists become real .xlsx rows and columns you can sort, filter and total. Honest note: tables are rebuilt from the PDF’s text layout, so simple tables come out clean while complex layouts may need a quick tidy-up in Excel.

About the source format (PDF):
PDFs freeze tables as fixed print layouts — the numbers are visible but locked away from formulas, sorting and filtering.

About the target format (Excel):
An Excel workbook sets the data free: real cells you can sort, filter, total and chart in Excel, Google Sheets or LibreOffice.

Use cases:
- Turning a bank statement PDF into a sortable spreadsheet
- Pulling invoice line-items into Excel for bookkeeping
- Extracting a supplier’s price list from a PDF for comparison

Tip: For the cleanest tables, use PDFs exported from Word, Excel or accounting software — those carry precise text positions. Scanned PDFs contain no text at all and can’t convert.

FAQs:
Q: How do I convert a PDF table to Excel for free?
A: Drop your PDF above and download a real .xlsx workbook — rows and columns reconstructed from the document’s text positions, ready to open in Excel, Google Sheets or LibreOffice. No sign-up, nothing uploaded.

Q: How accurate is the table reconstruction?
A: Best-effort, and honest about it: the tool reads where every word sits on the page and rebuilds rows and columns from those positions. Clean, simple tables — bank statements, invoices, price lists — usually come out ready to use. Multi-column magazine layouts, merged cells or skewed scans may need manual cleanup in Excel.

Q: Why do some cells merge or split incorrectly?
A: PDFs don’t store “this is a table” — only text plus coordinates. Wide gaps become column breaks; tightly packed text becomes one cell. When a PDF uses unusual spacing the guess can be off. The “one sheet per page” option and a quick once-over in Excel fix most cases.

Q: Can it convert a scanned PDF?
A: No — scanned PDFs are images of text with nothing to extract. They need OCR first, which the browser version doesn’t do yet. If you can select the text in your PDF, it will convert.

Q: Will it open password-protected PDFs?
A: No — remove the password first with the free Unlock PDF tool, then convert. Locked files can’t be opened by the converter.

Q: XLSX or CSV — which should I choose?
A: XLSX keeps multiple sheets and sensible column widths, and opens directly in Excel or Google Sheets. If you only need raw data for another program, the workbook imports cleanly there too.

### Edit PDF Online

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/edit-pdf/

What it does:
Click any text in your PDF and type to edit it — right on the page, in your browser. Fix typos in contracts, update a resume, correct figures in a report, then download the updated PDF. No uploads, no sign-up, no watermark.

About the source format (PDF):
PDFs are designed to look identical everywhere — which is exactly why their text is normally so hard to change without expensive desktop software.

About the target format (Edited PDF):
An edited PDF keeps the original layout and look, but with your corrections baked into the file — ready to send, print or archive.

Use cases:
- Fixing typos in a contract before signing it
- Updating your resume or CV in seconds
- Correcting names, dates or figures in a report

Tip: For long rewrites, switch to Text view — edit the whole page as plain text, then apply it back in one go.

FAQs:
Q: How can I edit text in a PDF for free?
A: Drop your PDF above. Every text block becomes clickable — click it, type your changes, and download the updated PDF with your edits baked in. It all happens in your browser: your file is never uploaded anywhere.

Q: Is my PDF uploaded to a server when I edit it?
A: Never. The editor runs 100% in your browser — the file is read, edited and rebuilt on your device. That is the whole point: private editing with nothing leaving your computer.

Q: Will the layout stay the same after editing?
A: For text-based PDFs, yes — only the words you edit are redrawn, at the exact same position and size. The cover box is painted in the sampled background color and your text in the sampled text color, so headers and colored sections keep their look. Redrawn text uses a matching font (Noto Sans for Noto-based PDFs, Helvetica otherwise). Longer replacement text grows its box to the right; nearby content never moves.

Q: What about scanned PDFs?
A: Scanned PDFs are pictures of text, not text — there is nothing clickable to edit. They need OCR first, which the browser version does not do yet.

Q: Can I edit images in the PDF?
A: Not yet — the editor works on text. Images pass through untouched into your downloaded file.

Q: What is the “clean PDF” download?
A: A rebuilt version of your document with flowing text and simple typography — handy when you made big edits and want a tidy, reflowed document instead of the original layout.

### Rotate PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/rotate-pdf/

What it does:
Fix sideways or upside-down PDF pages in seconds. Rotate all pages — or just pages 1-3, 5 — by 90°, 180° or 270°, right in your browser.

About the source format (PDF):
Scanned PDFs and phone exports often open sideways or upside-down, making them unreadable without tilting your head.

About the target format (PDF):
A rotated PDF opens correctly everywhere — the new orientation is baked into the file, not just your viewer.

Use cases:
- Fixing a scanned contract that opens sideways
- Straightening phone-scanned receipts before sending
- Flipping landscape slides back to portrait

Tip: Leave the page box empty to rotate every page; type "1-3, 5" to rotate only some.

FAQs:
Q: How do I rotate a PDF that opens sideways?
A: Drop the PDF, pick 90° clockwise (or 180° / 90° counter-clockwise), and optionally limit it to certain pages like "1-3, 5". Download the fixed PDF — the rotation is saved permanently.

Q: Is the rotation permanent?
A: Yes — the rotation is written into the PDF file itself, so it opens correctly in every reader, on every device.

Q: Can I rotate only some pages?
A: Yes. Type the pages in the Pages box (e.g. "1-3, 5") and only those rotate. Leave it blank to rotate the whole document.

Q: Does rotating reduce quality?
A: No. Rotation only changes page orientation metadata — your text and images are untouched, with zero quality loss.

Q: My PDF is upside down. Which option fixes it?
A: Choose 180°. Use 90° clockwise for pages lying on their side, 90° counter-clockwise if they lean the other way.

### Watermark PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/watermark-pdf/

What it does:
Stamp DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL or your brand across every PDF page. Diagonal text watermark with adjustable size and transparency — free, no sign-up.

About the source format (PDF):
Sharing unfinished or sensitive documents without a watermark invites misuse — anyone can pass them off as final.

About the target format (PDF):
A watermarked PDF carries your mark on every page: clear ownership, clear status, still perfectly readable underneath.

Use cases:
- Marking a proposal DRAFT before sending it out
- Stamping CONFIDENTIAL on internal reports
- Adding your brand name to free samples and portfolios

Tip: 25–40% opacity keeps the watermark visible without hurting readability. Go bolder only for "do not distribute" documents.

FAQs:
Q: How do I add a DRAFT watermark to a PDF?
A: Drop your PDF, type your watermark text (e.g. DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL), pick a size and transparency, and download. The watermark is stamped diagonally across every page.

Q: Can I control how strong the watermark looks?
A: Yes — set the opacity from 5% (barely-there) to 90% (impossible to miss), plus three text sizes. 25% is the sweet spot for drafts.

Q: Where does the watermark appear?
A: Diagonally across the center of every page, behind nothing and over everything — visible on all pages at once.

Q: Will the watermark cover my text?
A: It sits over the page but at partial transparency, so your content stays readable underneath. Lower the opacity if it feels heavy.

Q: Can I remove a watermark later?
A: A stamped watermark becomes part of the PDF — that is the point. Keep an unstamped copy if you will need a clean version later.

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/page-numbers-pdf/

FAQs:
Q: How do I add page numbers to a PDF?

Q: What format do the numbers use?
A: "Page 1 of 12" — total count included, so readers always know how far along they are.

Q: Can I choose where the numbers appear?
A: Yes: bottom center, bottom left, bottom right, top center, or top right — five positions.

Q: Will it cover my content?
A: Numbers sit in the margin area in small grey type, well clear of typical content. If your pages run edge-to-edge, pick a top position.

Q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
A: Yes — page numbers are drawn onto the page regardless of whether the content is text or scanned images.

### Unlock PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/unlock-pdf/

What it does:
Remove the password from a PDF you own. Enter the password once — it never leaves your browser — and download a freely usable copy.

About the source format (PDF):
Password-protected PDFs you legitimately own become a daily friction: every open, print, or merge demands the password again.

About the target format (PDF):
An unlocked copy opens instantly everywhere — same pages, no more password prompts.

Use cases:
- Removing the password from your own bank statements for archiving
- Unlocking a protected ebook you bought so it opens on every device
- Preparing a locked PDF for merging or editing

Tip: You must know the password — no tool can (or should) crack a password you do not have.

FAQs:
Q: How do I remove a password from a PDF?
A: Drop the locked PDF, type its password, and download the unlocked copy. Your password is used once inside your browser and never stored or sent anywhere.

Q: Is my password safe?
A: Yes. It is typed into your own browser, used once to open the file, and never stored, logged, or uploaded. The file never leaves your device either.

Q: What if I forgot the password?
A: Then it cannot be unlocked — that is what the password is for. Contact whoever set it.

Q: Will the unlocked PDF look the same?
A: Pages are rebuilt as high-quality images, so the look is preserved — but text is no longer selectable or searchable. For full fidelity, ask the document owner for an unprotected original.

Q: Does it remove print/copy restrictions too?
A: Yes — the rebuilt copy carries no passwords and no restrictions.

### Extract Images from PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/extract-images-pdf/

What it does:
Pull every embedded photo and graphic out of a PDF as PNG files. Download them individually or all at once as a ZIP — original resolution kept.

About the source format (PDF):
Photos trapped inside PDFs cannot be right-click-saved — screenshots are the usual sad workaround, at screen resolution.

About the target format (Images):
Extracted PNGs are the real embedded files at full resolution — ready to reuse, edit, or archive.

Use cases:
- Recovering product photos from a supplier catalogue PDF
- Pulling charts out of a report for a presentation
- Saving illustrations from an ebook

Tip: If a "photo" does not appear, it is probably vector clip-art (drawn shapes), not an embedded image — those cannot be extracted as files.

FAQs:
Q: How do I save pictures from a PDF?
A: Drop the PDF and every embedded image is listed for download as a PNG — grab them one by one or take them all as a ZIP. Images come out at their original embedded resolution.

Q: What quality are the extracted images?
A: Original embedded resolution — whatever the PDF author put in. No re-compression, no screenshots.

Q: What format do I get?
A: PNG files, named by page and image number (e.g. report-p2-img1.png), or all of them in one ZIP.

Q: Why is an image missing?
A: Only true embedded raster images extract. Vector drawings, icons, and backgrounds drawn with shapes are not image files.

Q: Is there a limit?
A: No file-count limit — a 200-image catalogue extracts just fine, though very large PDFs take a moment.

### Redact PDF

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/redact-pdf/

What it does:
Black out names, ID numbers, or any sensitive words across a whole PDF at once. Type the words — every occurrence gets covered.

About the source format (PDF):
Sharing documents with visible personal data — names, ID numbers, salaries — is a privacy accident waiting to happen.

About the target format (PDF):
A redacted PDF hides every listed term behind black boxes, safe to share or publish.

Use cases:
- Hiding ID numbers before sharing a document publicly
- Redacting names from a report for blind review
- Covering salaries in a shared HR export

Tip: List every variant ("John", "J. Smith") — matching is literal, so think like a finder, not a reader.

FAQs:
Q: How do I black out text in a PDF?
A: Drop the PDF, type the words or phrases to hide (comma or line separated), and download. Every occurrence on every page is covered with a solid black box.

Q: Is the redaction permanent and secure?
A: Honest answer: this is visual redaction — the words are covered with black boxes, but the underlying text data remains in the file. For legally watertight redaction (court filings, medical records), use desktop software that strips the data too.

Q: Is matching case-sensitive?
A: No — "Secret", "SECRET" and "secret" are all caught.

Q: Can I redact phrases, not just single words?
A: Yes — type full phrases like "Project Nightingale". Each phrase is matched wherever it appears on one line.

Q: What about scanned PDFs?
A: Scanned pages are images, not text — there is nothing to match. Those need OCR first, which the browser version does not do yet.

## Image Converters

Free online image converters that run entirely in your browser. Change PNG to JPG, WebP to PNG, HEIC to JPG and more — resize and rotate images in bulk, or create PNG to PDF, JPG to PDF, WebP to PDF, GIF to PDF, BMP to PDF and HEIC to PDF documents — your photos are never uploaded anywhere.

### PNG to JPG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/png-to-jpg/

What it does:
Turn PNG screenshots, logos and graphics into much smaller JPG files. Perfect when a PNG is too big to email or upload — same picture, a fraction of the size.

About the source format (PNG):
PNG stores every pixel losslessly, which keeps screenshots and logos razor-sharp. The trade-off is size — PNGs are often several megabytes, too heavy for email attachments and quick uploads.

About the target format (JPG):
JPG is the world’s most compatible image format. Its lossy compression squeezes photos and graphics down to a fraction of their size, and it opens on every phone, computer, website and app ever made.

Use cases:
- Emailing screenshots without hitting attachment size limits
- Converting PNG graphics for upload forms that only accept JPG
- Shrinking website images for faster page loads

Tip: PNG transparency becomes a white background in JPG. If your image has a transparent background you need to keep, convert to WebP instead.

FAQs:
Q: Will converting PNG to JPG reduce quality?
A: JPG uses lossy compression, so files get dramatically smaller with only a tiny, usually invisible quality change. If your PNG has transparency, note that JPG does not support it — transparent areas become white.

Q: What quality setting is used for the JPG?
A: High quality (92%) — screenshots and graphics look identical to the PNG while files shrink 60–80%.

Q: Can I convert back to PNG later?
A: Yes, but the small JPG quality loss is permanent. Keep the original PNG if pixel-perfection might matter later.

Q: Why is JPG better for email?
A: Email providers cap attachment sizes — a 5 MB PNG often becomes a 700 KB JPG that sails through.

Q: Does it work for photos too?
A: Absolutely — though photos usually start as JPG already. This converter shines on PNG screenshots, logos and graphics.

### PNG to WebP Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/png-to-webp/

What it does:
Convert PNG images to WebP, the modern format that keeps transparency while shrinking files by 25–35%. Ideal for faster websites and smaller uploads.

About the source format (PNG):
PNG is the default for crisp screenshots and graphics because it never degrades quality. But it barely compresses, so PNG files are bulky — a real problem on the web.

About the target format (WebP):
WebP is Google’s modern image format: 25–35% smaller than PNG or JPG at the same visual quality, with transparency support. Every modern browser displays it natively.

Use cases:
- Speeding up a website by replacing PNG images with WebP
- Keeping screenshot transparency while cutting file size
- Preparing images for platforms that prefer WebP uploads

Tip: Compare the WebP side-by-side with your PNG at 100% zoom — you won’t see a difference, but the file will be roughly a third of the size.

FAQs:
Q: Why convert PNG to WebP instead of JPG?
A: WebP keeps transparency like PNG but compresses far better — typically 25–35% smaller than PNG and even smaller than JPG at similar quality. All modern browsers display WebP natively.

Q: Will the WebP keep my PNG’s transparency?
A: Yes — unlike JPG, WebP fully supports transparency, so logos and UI graphics convert perfectly.

Q: Do all browsers support WebP now?
A: All modern ones do — Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari 14+ and every mobile browser from recent years. Only truly ancient browsers miss it.

### PNG to AVIF Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/png-to-avif/

What it does:
Convert PNG to AVIF, the cutting-edge image format with the best compression available today. Great for web developers squeezing every kilobyte.

About the source format (PNG):
PNG preserves images pixel-for-pixel, transparency included. That perfection is expensive in bandwidth — a single PNG screenshot can outweigh an entire page of text.

About the target format (AVIF):
AVIF is the newest image format, squeezing 20–30% smaller files than even WebP at the same quality. Best when every kilobyte counts and your audience uses modern browsers.

Use cases:
- Maximum compression for hero images on performance-critical sites
- Archiving graphics at the smallest size without visible loss
- Testing next-gen formats for a portfolio or tech blog

Tip: AVIF encoding needs a recent browser (Chrome or Edge recommended). If you see a ‘not supported’ message, WebP is the safe fallback at nearly the same size.

FAQs:
Q: My browser says AVIF is not supported. What now?
A: AVIF encoding needs a recent browser — Chrome or Edge work best. If yours does not support it, convert to WebP instead: nearly as small and supported everywhere.

Q: Is AVIF better than WebP?
A: For compression, yes — typically 20–30% smaller at equal quality. For compatibility, WebP still wins. Use AVIF when your audience is on modern browsers.

Q: Why does AVIF conversion take longer?
A: AVIF’s superior compression comes from heavier math — encoding takes a few seconds longer than WebP, but viewing the result is instant.

### JPG to PNG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/jpg-to-png/

What it does:
Convert JPG photos to PNG when you need lossless quality or plan to edit further. Note: this will not restore quality already lost to JPG compression — but it stops further loss.

About the source format (JPG):
JPG is the universal photo format — tiny files that open everywhere. Its lossy compression is tuned for photos, but every re-save shaves off a little more quality.

About the target format (PNG):
PNG is completely lossless: once your image is a PNG, editing and re-saving it never degrades it further. The safe format for graphics you plan to keep editing.

Use cases:
- Freezing a JPG at its current quality before heavy editing
- Converting photos for software that requires PNG input
- Preparing images for print workflows that prefer lossless files

Tip: Converting JPG to PNG stops further quality loss, but it can’t restore detail the JPG already discarded — and the PNG will be much bigger.

FAQs:
Q: Does JPG to PNG improve image quality?
A: No — conversion cannot recover detail that JPG compression already removed. But PNG is lossless, so editing and re-saving a PNG will not degrade it further the way re-saving a JPG does.

Q: Will my photo look better as a PNG?
A: No — conversion can’t invent detail that JPG compression removed. The benefit is that future edits and saves won’t degrade it further.

Q: Why is the PNG so much bigger?
A: PNG stores every pixel exactly with no lossy shortcuts. Expect 3–5x the JPG’s file size — that’s the price of lossless.

WebP is the modern replacement for JPG on the web: noticeably smaller files at identical visual quality, supported by every current browser.

A: 25–35% smaller at the same visual quality is typical — a 900 KB photo often becomes about 600 KB.

A: Yes — all modern browsers support it. Only worry if your audience includes Internet Explorer, which is vanishingly rare now.

### HEIC to JPG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/heic-to-jpg/

What it does:
Convert iPhone HEIC photos to JPG so they open everywhere — Windows, Android, email and the web. The fix for "my iPhone photo will not upload".

About the source format (HEIC):
HEIC is Apple’s efficient photo format — roughly half the size of JPG at the same quality. iPhones have saved photos as HEIC by default since 2017.

About the target format (JPG):
JPG is the universal fallback: bigger than HEIC, but readable by every device, app and website on earth.

Use cases:
- Emailing iPhone photos to people on Windows
- Uploading to websites and forms that reject HEIC files
- Sharing in WhatsApp or Telegram without compatibility warnings
- Saving photos in a format every device will still open in ten years

FAQs:
Q: Why do my iPhone photos need converting?
A: iPhones save photos as HEIC by default, which many Windows apps, websites and older devices cannot open. Converting to JPG makes the photo universally compatible.

Q: Why won’t my HEIC photo open on Windows?
A: Windows needs an extra paid HEVC codec to open HEIC, and most PCs don’t have it. Converting to JPG sidesteps the problem entirely — JPG opens everywhere with no extra software.

Q: Will converting HEIC to JPG lose quality?
A: Barely. We convert at high quality (92%), so any difference is invisible in normal viewing. Your original HEIC file is never touched — the JPG is a new download.

Q: Can I convert several HEIC photos at once?
A: Right now each conversion handles one file at a time — drop a photo, convert, download, repeat. It takes a few seconds per photo.

Q: How do I stop my iPhone saving HEIC in the future?
A: On your iPhone go to Settings → Camera → Formats and choose "Most Compatible". New photos will save as JPG — but this won’t change photos you already took.

Q: Does this work for HEIC files from cameras or drones, not just iPhones?
A: Yes — any valid HEIC or HEIF file converts the same way, no matter which device created it.

Q: HEIC to PNG or HEIC to JPG?
A: PNG for editing, printing and archiving (lossless, larger). JPG for sharing and everyday use (smaller, still excellent).

Q: Does the PNG keep the photo’s full resolution?
A: Yes — every pixel converts at full resolution. Nothing is downscaled.

### HEIF to JPG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/heif-to-jpg/

What it does:
Convert HEIF images to JPG for universal compatibility. Same idea as HEIC — HEIF is simply the format name without the "container" distinction.

About the source format (HEIF):
HEIF is the underlying standard behind Apple’s HEIC photos — extremely efficient, but unreadable by most Windows apps and websites.

About the target format (JPG):
JPG is the universal fallback: slightly bigger than HEIF, but opens absolutely everywhere.

Use cases:
- Opening HEIF images on a Windows PC
- Uploading HEIF photos to web forms
- Sharing HEIF images with Android users

Tip: HEIC and HEIF are siblings — if your iPhone file says .HEIF instead of .HEIC, this is the right converter.

FAQs:
Q: What is the difference between HEIC and HEIF?
A: HEIF is the format standard; HEIC is HEIF using HEVC compression — what iPhones actually produce. Both open the same way here: drop the file and convert.

Q: What’s the difference between HEIC and HEIF?
A: HEIF is the format standard; HEIC is HEIF using HEVC compression — what iPhones actually produce. Both convert the same way here.

Q: Will I lose quality?
A: A negligible amount at high quality — invisible in normal viewing. The original file is never modified.

### HEIF to PNG Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/heif-to-png/

What it does:
Convert HEIF images to lossless PNG for editing and archiving without any further quality loss.

About the source format (HEIF):
HEIF packs photos incredibly small using modern compression. The price of that efficiency: most non-Apple software can’t open it.

About the target format (PNG):
PNG trades file size for universality and lossless quality — the safe, editable, archivable result.

Use cases:
- Editing HEIF photos in desktop software
- Converting HEIF for a design project
- Lossless archiving of HEIF originals

Tip: Expect the PNG to be several times larger than your HEIF — HEIF is one of the most efficient formats ever made.

FAQs:
Q: Will the PNG be much bigger than my HEIF?
A: Yes — HEIF is extremely efficient, so the PNG will be several times larger. That is the price of a lossless, universally editable file.

Q: Why is the PNG so much bigger than my HEIF?
A: HEIF’s compression is state-of-the-art; PNG is lossless and much older. A 4–6x size gap is normal.

Q: Should I keep the original HEIF too?
A: If storage allows, yes — it’s your smallest full-quality original. The PNG is your editable working copy.

Q: Can I combine several BMPs into one PDF?

### Rotate Images

Q: Why do my photos open sideways in some apps?

Q: Does it keep my file format?
A: Yes — JPG stays JPG, PNG stays PNG, per file.

Q: Can I rotate just one image?
A: Of course — drop one file and it works exactly the same.

## Data Converters

Free online data-format converters for developers and analysts. Convert JSON to CSV, CSV to JSON, JSON to YAML, YAML to JSON, TOML to JSON and XML to JSON — or turn a CSV spreadsheet into a printable PDF table — parsed locally, never uploaded.

### JSON to CSV Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/json-to-csv/

What it does:
Convert a JSON array of objects into a CSV spreadsheet that opens in Excel and Google Sheets. The fastest way to make API data human-readable.

About the source format (JSON):
JSON is the data format of APIs and JavaScript — nested, precise, and unreadable to non-developers.

About the target format (CSV):
CSV is the spreadsheet format: rows and columns that open in Excel and Google Sheets, readable by anyone.

Use cases:
- Turning API responses into a spreadsheet for analysis
- Sharing JSON data with colleagues who use Excel
- Preparing data for tools that import CSV

Tip: Works best with an array of objects sharing the same keys — each object becomes one spreadsheet row.

FAQs:
Q: What shape of JSON works best?
A: An array of objects with consistent keys — like [{"name":"A"},{"name":"B"}]. A single object also works; it becomes a one-row CSV.

Q: What if my JSON is nested?
A: Nested objects are flattened with dot notation (address.city), so no data is lost — though deep nesting is easier to read as JSON.

Q: How are commas inside values handled?
A: Properly quoted per CSV rules — values with commas or quotes are wrapped so spreadsheets parse them correctly.

### CSV to JSON Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/csv-to-json/

What it does:
Convert a CSV spreadsheet into structured JSON for APIs, scripts and databases. Handles quoted fields and commas inside cells correctly.

About the source format (CSV):
CSV is how the world shares tabular data — simple, but dumb: no types, no structure beyond rows.

About the target format (JSON):
JSON gives that data structure: typed values, nesting, and a format every API and programming language understands.

Use cases:
- Feeding spreadsheet data into a web app or API
- Converting exports for a JavaScript project
- Turning CSV logs into structured JSON for processing

Tip: The first row becomes your JSON keys — make sure your CSV has a clean header row before converting.

FAQs:
Q: Does the first row become the keys?
A: Yes — the header row becomes the JSON keys, and every following row becomes an object. Empty headers get safe names like column_1.

Q: Are numbers kept as numbers?
A: Yes — numeric cells become JSON numbers, not strings, so your data stays computable.

Q: What about empty cells?
A: Empty cells become null, preserving the row structure without inventing data.

### JSON to YAML Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/json-to-yaml/

What it does:
Convert JSON config into readable YAML for Docker Compose, Kubernetes, CI pipelines and app settings.

About the source format (JSON):
JSON is precise but noisy — braces, quotes and commas everywhere make it tiring to read and edit by hand.

About the target format (YAML):
YAML is the human-friendly config format: clean indentation, no clutter — the native language of Docker Compose and Kubernetes.

Use cases:
- Converting JSON configs for Kubernetes manifests
- Making API data editable as a config file
- Preparing Docker Compose files from JSON sources

Tip: Watch indentation in the YAML output — YAML is whitespace-sensitive, unlike JSON.

FAQs:
Q: Why convert JSON to YAML?
A: YAML is far easier for humans to read and edit than JSON — no braces or quotes everywhere. Most DevOps tools accept YAML configs natively.

Q: Is YAML just prettier JSON?
A: Mostly — YAML is a superset of JSON, so data converts exactly. The win is readability.

Q: Can YAML do everything JSON can?
A: For data, yes. Note that comments can’t round-trip back to JSON, since JSON has no comments.

### YAML to JSON Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/yaml-to-json/

What it does:
Convert YAML config files to JSON for APIs, JavaScript apps and tools that only speak JSON.

About the source format (YAML):
YAML is great for humans editing configs — but most APIs, and all of JavaScript’s native tooling, speak JSON.

About the target format (JSON):
JSON is the machine format: strict, unambiguous, parseable by every language’s standard library.

Use cases:
- Converting Kubernetes configs for programmatic processing
- Turning YAML settings into JSON for a JS app
- Validating YAML by viewing it as strict JSON

Tip: Anchors and aliases in YAML are resolved during conversion — the JSON holds the final expanded values.

FAQs:
Q: Will comments in my YAML survive?
A: No — JSON has no comments, so they are dropped. The data itself converts exactly, including nested objects and arrays.

Q: Do YAML comments survive?
A: No — JSON has no comment syntax, so comments are dropped. The data converts exactly.

Q: What happens to multi-line strings?
A: They become JSON strings with escaped line breaks — the breaks are preserved, just encoded.

### TOML to JSON Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/toml-to-json/

What it does:
Convert TOML config files (Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml and friends) into JSON for processing in any language.

About the source format (TOML):
TOML is the config format of Rust’s Cargo, Python’s pyproject.toml and many modern tools — minimal, obvious, and typed.

About the target format (JSON):
JSON makes that config readable by any language or tool without a TOML parser.

Use cases:
- Reading pyproject.toml data in a JavaScript tool
- Converting Cargo.toml for analysis scripts
- Bridging TOML configs into JSON-based pipelines

Tip: TOML dates convert to ISO strings in JSON — parse them with your language’s date handling.

FAQs:
Q: What is TOML used for?
A: TOML is the config format behind Rust's Cargo, Python's pyproject.toml and many other tools. Converting to JSON makes it easy to read programmatically.

Q: What is TOML mainly used for?
A: Configuration files — most famously Cargo.toml (Rust) and pyproject.toml (Python). It’s designed to be obvious to humans.

Q: Does anything get lost?
A: TOML’s types — integers, floats, booleans, datetimes, arrays, tables — all map cleanly to JSON. Only comments are dropped.

### XML to JSON Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/xml-to-json/

What it does:
Convert XML documents into clean JSON. Attributes are kept under @attributes so nothing is lost in translation.

About the source format (XML):
XML is the venerable data format of enterprises, RSS feeds and Office files — verbose, but structured.

About the target format (JSON):
JSON is XML’s lean successor for data exchange: the same structure with a fraction of the noise.

Use cases:
- Converting RSS/XML feeds for a JavaScript app
- Modernizing legacy XML exports
- Turning SOAP-style responses into workable JSON

Tip: Check the @attributes objects in the output — that’s where XML attributes live, so nothing is silently dropped.

FAQs:
Q: How are XML attributes handled?
A: Attributes are preserved in an "@attributes" object, repeated elements become arrays, and text content lands in "#text" — so the JSON round-trips your data faithfully.

Q: How are repeated elements handled?
A: They become JSON arrays automatically — an <item> repeated three times becomes an array of three objects.

Q: What about XML namespaces?
A: Namespace prefixes stay in the key names (e.g. dc:title), so namespaced documents remain distinguishable.

### CSV to PDF Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/csv-to-pdf/

What it does:
Turn a CSV spreadsheet into a printable PDF table — header row highlighted, grid lines, columns auto-sized. Your data as a proper document.

CSV is the universal spreadsheet exchange format — but raw CSV is not something you print or email to a client.

About the target format (PDF):
PDF turns your spreadsheet into a formatted, printable table document that looks deliberate and professional.

- Printing a CSV export as a readable report
- Emailing spreadsheet data to someone without Excel
- Archiving data exports as fixed-layout documents

FAQs:
Q: How does the table look?
A: A clean A4 table: bold header row on a shaded background, thin grid lines, and columns automatically sized to their content. Multi-page for long spreadsheets.

Q: What if my CSV has many columns?
A: Columns shrink automatically to fit the page, down to a readable minimum. Very wide sheets stay legible; extremely wide ones may need fewer columns.

Q: Are commas inside cells handled?
A: Yes — quoted fields with commas or quotes inside parse correctly, so your data lands in the right columns.

Q: How many rows can it handle?
A: Up to 500 rows per conversion, flowing across as many pages as needed. Larger exports: split the CSV first.

## Subtitle Converters

Free online subtitle converters. Switch SRT to WebVTT for the web, to ASS for styled karaoke subtitles, or between any of SRT, VTT, ASS and SSA — all in your browser.

### SRT to WebVTT Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/srt-to-vtt/

What it does:
Convert SRT subtitles to WebVTT for HTML5 video players. VTT is the web standard — required for <track> captions that work in every browser.

About the source format (SRT):
SRT is the universal subtitle format — plain numbered cues with timestamps. Nearly every player and platform accepts it.

About the target format (WebVTT):
WebVTT is the web’s caption standard: the only format browsers accept natively for video captions via the track element.

Use cases:
- Adding captions to an HTML5 video player
- Publishing accessible video on the web
- Converting subtitles for web embedding

Tip: Name the .vtt file the same as your video and add a captions track — browsers pick it up automatically.

FAQs:
Q: Why do I need WebVTT instead of SRT?
A: Browsers only accept WebVTT for native <video> captions via the <track> element. SRT will not load there — this conversion fixes that in one click.

Q: Do I need to change the timestamps?
A: No — timestamps convert precisely; only the header format and separators change.

Q: Can I style WebVTT captions?
A: Yes — WebVTT supports basic styling with ::cue CSS, unlike SRT. The text converts first; style it afterwards.

### WebVTT to SRT Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/vtt-to-srt/

What it does:
Convert WebVTT captions back to SRT, the universal subtitle format that video players, editors and YouTube all accept.

About the source format (WebVTT):
WebVTT powers web video captions, but outside browsers it’s the odd one out — many desktop players and editors prefer SRT.

About the target format (SRT):
SRT is the lingua franca of subtitles: YouTube, VLC, Premiere and virtually everything else accept it.

Use cases:
- Using web captions in VLC or another desktop player
- Uploading captions to platforms that want SRT
- Editing web captions in subtitle software

Tip: Styling tags like <b> are stripped since SRT is plain text — timing and dialogue stay exact.

FAQs:
Q: Do I lose anything converting VTT to SRT?
A: Styling tags (like <b> or <i>) are stripped since SRT is plain text — but timing and text stay exactly the same.

Q: Will I lose the caption positioning?
A: Yes — SRT has no positioning, so VTT position cues are dropped. Text and timing are preserved.

Q: Is SRT still relevant?
A: Very — it’s the most widely supported subtitle format in existence, which is exactly why people convert to it.

### SRT to ASS Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/srt-to-ass/

What it does:
Convert SRT to ASS for styled subtitles — custom fonts, colors, positioning and karaoke effects that SRT cannot do.

About the source format (SRT):
SRT handles plain dialogue well, but it’s style-blind: no fonts, no colors, no positioning.

About the target format (ASS):
ASS (Advanced SubStation Alpha) is the styled subtitle format — fonts, colors, screen positions, outlines and karaoke effects.

Use cases:
- Styling fansub releases with custom fonts
- Creating karaoke-timed lyrics
- Positioning dialogue for overlapping speakers

Tip: Your text and timing carry over; open the ASS in Aegisub to apply styles — that’s where ASS shines.

FAQs:
Q: What does ASS give me that SRT does not?
A: Styling: fonts, colors, screen position, outlines and karaoke timing. Your text and timing carry over; you can then style it in Aegisub or any ASS editor.

Q: What’s the difference between ASS and SSA?
A: ASS is the newer, more capable version. SSA is its predecessor — pick ASS unless a specific old tool demands SSA.

Q: Will my video player show the styles?
A: VLC, MPV and most anime players render ASS styles fully. Some smart TVs and phones may show plain text.

A: Styling codes are removed — SRT cannot carry them. The dialogue text and its exact timing are preserved.

A: No — every line of dialogue converts with its timing. Only fonts, colors and positioning are dropped.

About the source format (MP4):

About the target format (MP3):
MP3 is the universal audio format: tiny files that play on every device, car stereo and app ever made.

Use cases:
- Saving podcast audio from a video file

Tip: We encode at 192 kbps — transparent quality for music and voice, at roughly 1.4 MB per minute.

FAQs:

A: 192 kbps MP3 — transparent quality for music and voice that sounds identical to the original for the vast majority of listeners.

Q: What audio quality do I get?
A: 192 kbps MP3 — indistinguishable from the original for the vast majority of listeners, including music.

Q: How big will the MP3 be?
A: About 1.4 MB per minute of audio. A 10-minute video’s audio becomes roughly a 14 MB MP3.

Q: Can I extract audio from a 2-hour video?
A: Yes, as long as the file stays under ~500 MB — beyond that browsers tend to run out of memory.

Q: Does it keep the video too?
A: No — the video track is discarded and only the audio is kept. That’s exactly what makes the file so much smaller.

Q: Will I lose quality?

Free online audio converters. Turn WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A, AAC or WMA into universal MP3s at 192 kbps, or convert MP3 back to WAV — all on your device, nothing uploaded.

### WAV to MP3 Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/wav-to-mp3/

What it does:
Convert huge WAV files to compact MP3s at 192 kbps — about 7x smaller with no audible difference.

About the source format (WAV):
WAV is uncompressed CD-quality audio — perfect fidelity, enormous files (about 10 MB per minute).

About the target format (MP3):
MP3 at 192 kbps keeps that audio sounding identical to almost every ear at roughly one-seventh the size.

Use cases:
- Shrinking WAV recordings for sharing
- Converting studio exports for streaming
- Making voice memos emailable

Tip: 192 kbps is the sweet spot — below 128 kbps you’d start hearing the difference on music.

FAQs:
Q: Will I hear a difference?
A: Almost certainly not — 192 kbps MP3 is transparent for the vast majority of listeners, even on good headphones.

Q: Will I hear a difference?
A: Almost certainly not — 192 kbps MP3 is transparent for the vast majority of listeners, even on good headphones.

Q: How much smaller?
A: Roughly 7x smaller. A 50 MB WAV becomes about a 7 MB MP3.

### FLAC to MP3 Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/flac-to-mp3/

What it does:
Convert lossless FLAC music to universal MP3 for car stereos, phones and anywhere FLAC won’t play.

About the source format (FLAC):
FLAC is audiophile-grade lossless compression — bit-perfect, but still 5x bigger than MP3.

About the target format (MP3):
MP3 trades inaudible detail for universal compatibility and tiny files.

Use cases:
- Making FLAC music playable in the car
- Converting a FLAC library for a phone with limited storage
- Sharing lossless rips with friends

Tip: Keep your FLAC originals archived — convert copies to MP3 for portable use.

FAQs:
Q: Isn’t FLAC better than MP3?
A: Technically yes — FLAC is lossless. But in blind tests almost nobody can tell 192 kbps MP3 from FLAC. Compatibility and size are MP3’s wins.

Q: Isn’t FLAC better than MP3?
A: Technically yes — FLAC is lossless. But in blind tests almost nobody can tell 192 kbps MP3 from FLAC. Compatibility and size are MP3’s wins.

Q: Do tags (artist, album) survive?
A: Yes — metadata tags carry over to the MP3.

### OGG to MP3 Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/ogg-to-mp3/

What it does:
Convert OGG Vorbis audio to MP3 for playback on iPhones, car stereos and everything that ignores OGG.

About the source format (OGG):
OGG Vorbis is the open-source audio codec — great quality, but spotty support on Apple devices and car stereos.

About the target format (MP3):
MP3 plays on literally everything with an audio chip.

Use cases:
- Playing OGG music on an iPhone
- Converting game audio rips for general use
- Making OGG files car-stereo compatible

Tip: OGG and MP3 at similar bitrates sound the same — this conversion is purely about compatibility.

FAQs:
Q: Where do OGG files come from?
A: Spotify’s local files, many video games, and open-source projects. OGG is excellent — just not universal.

Q: Where do OGG files come from?
A: Spotify’s local files, many video games, and open-source projects. It’s excellent — just not universal.

Q: Quality loss?
A: Negligible at 192 kbps. You’re transcoding between two good lossy codecs; the difference is inaudible to nearly everyone.

### M4A to MP3 Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/m4a-to-mp3/

What it does:
Convert Apple M4A audio to MP3 for old MP3 players, DJ software and maximum compatibility.

About the source format (M4A):
M4A (AAC) is Apple’s audio format — the iTunes default. Great quality, but some older players and DJ software want MP3.

About the target format (MP3):
MP3 is the safe universal audio format nothing rejects.

Use cases:
- Converting iTunes purchases for old MP3 players
- Preparing audio for DJ software that prefers MP3
- Standardizing a mixed audio library

Tip: M4A/AAC is technically slightly more efficient than MP3 — but at 192 kbps the difference is inaudible, and compatibility wins.

FAQs:
Q: Is M4A better than MP3?
A: Marginally more efficient at the same bitrate. In practice 192 kbps of either sounds identical — pick based on compatibility.

Q: Is M4A better than MP3?
A: Marginally more efficient at the same bitrate. In practice 192 kbps of either sounds identical — pick based on compatibility.

Q: Do protected iTunes files convert?
A: Old DRM-protected M4P files won’t. Standard DRM-free M4A converts fine.

MP3 remains the compatibility baseline every device supports.

Use cases:
- Converting AAC streams for legacy hardware

FAQs:
Q: AAC vs MP3 quality?

### MP3 to WAV Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/mp3-to-wav/

What it does:
Convert MP3 to uncompressed WAV for editing in a DAW or any pro audio workflow that demands WAV.

About the source format (MP3):
MP3 is the compact universal format — but it’s lossy, and some pro workflows demand uncompressed audio.

About the target format (WAV):
WAV is uncompressed PCM: the studio standard that every DAW and audio tool accepts.

Use cases:
- Preparing MP3 for editing in a DAW
- Converting MP3 for audio software that needs WAV
- Making MP3s CD-burn ready

Tip: This won’t restore quality the MP3 discarded — it just gives you an uncompressed container for editing.

FAQs:
Q: Will it sound better as WAV?
A: No — conversion can’t recover what MP3 compression removed. The benefit is compatibility with pro tools, not quality.

Q: Will it sound better as WAV?
A: No — conversion can’t recover what MP3 compression removed. The benefit is compatibility with pro tools, not quality.

Q: Why is the WAV so big?
A: Uncompressed audio is ~10 MB per minute. That’s normal — it’s the price of the studio standard.

### OGG to WAV Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/ogg-to-wav/

What it does:
Convert OGG audio to uncompressed WAV for editors, samplers and game engines that only accept WAV.

About the source format (OGG):
OGG Vorbis is efficient and open — but pro audio tools and some game engines want plain WAV.

About the target format (WAV):
WAV is the uncompressed interchange format: no codec, no patents, no surprises.

Use cases:
- Converting game audio OGGs for editing
- Preparing OGG for sample libraries
- Getting OGG into WAV-only software

Tip: Like all lossy-to-lossless conversions, quality stays exactly as good as the OGG — no better, no worse.

FAQs:
Q: Does WAV improve OGG quality?
A: No — it preserves it exactly. The WAV is bigger, not better. The point is compatibility with WAV-only software.

Q: Does WAV improve OGG quality?
A: No — it preserves it exactly. The WAV is bigger, not better. The point is compatibility with WAV-only software.

Q: Why would I want that?
A: Some audio editors, samplers and game engines only accept WAV. This conversion is the bridge.

### WMA to MP3 Converter

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/wma-to-mp3/

What it does:
Convert old Windows WMA rips to MP3 — rescuing 2000s music collections for modern playback.

About the source format (WMA):
WMA is Microsoft’s 2000s-era audio format — once bundled with Windows Media Player, now largely abandoned.

About the target format (MP3):
MP3 brings that audio into the modern world of universal playback.

Use cases:
- Converting old Windows Media rips
- Rescuing a WMA music collection

FAQs:
Q: Where do WMA files come from?

Q: Where do WMA files come from?
A: Windows Media Player CD rips from the 2000s. If you ripped CDs on Windows back then, you probably have WMAs.

Q: Why won’t my WMA convert?
A: If it was bought from an old DRM music store, it’s locked. Plain ripped WMAs convert fine.

### Merge Audio

URL: https://allinoneconverter.vercel.app/convert/merge-audios/

What it does:
Join audio clips into one MP3 — podcast segments, voice memos, or music parts. Arrange the order, pick a bitrate, and download a single seamless file.

About the source format (Audio):
Voice memos, interview segments and music ideas pile up as separate files — hard to share or play in order.

About the target format (MP3):
One merged MP3 plays seamlessly and shares like any single audio file.

Use cases:
- Joining podcast segments into one episode
- Combining voice memos into a single recording
- Merging music stems or practice takes

Tip: MP3 segments join with no re-encoding (no quality loss). Mixed formats are converted to MP3 at your chosen bitrate.

FAQs:
Q: How do I join voice memos into one file?
A: Drop your recordings in order, rearrange with the arrows if needed, choose a bitrate, and download one MP3. Everything runs in your browser.

Q: Does merging MP3s lose quality?
A: No — MP3 segments join via stream copy with zero re-encoding. Only non-MP3 inputs get encoded once.

Q: Which bitrate should I choose?
A: 192 kbps is the sweet spot for voice and most music. 320 kbps for critical listening, 128 kbps for the smallest files.
